overall_reason: The fixed 1920 slide holds its copy, but the Chinese runs set in Latin-only stacks fall back to SimSun and half the slide's text needs script to appear.

score.reason: T-SCRIPT-COVERAGE fails (ROB-014: SimSun draws Chinese in 9 nodes) and T-NO-SCRIPT fails on the step lists (ROB-015); T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB passes at 152 KiB.

findings.title: Each language and script is declared and has its face
findings.where: Kicker, panel names, step text and reaction line (div.kicker, span.name, span.text, span.reaction), 1920px, tiles/1920-00.png
findings.evidence: fonts.nodes_with_glyphs_from_an_undeclared_face: 'A real task from yesterday · 一个昨晚刚发生的真实场景。' declares "Source Serif 4", serif and SimSun drew 13 glyphs; '「呃，能用，但…」' 14 SimSun glyphs; '检查点 1：先答四问' 8; '通用 AI / Agent' 2; 'huashu-design 启动后' 3. Even nodes that declare "Noto Serif SC" ('没有问任何问题', 11 glyphs; the scene title, 9 glyphs) were drawn partly by SimSun. families_drawn lists SimSun at 139 glyphs and NSimSun at 11.
findings.before: Chinese words inside Latin serif stacks, and characters missing from the loaded Noto Serif SC subset, fall back to the system face.
findings.after: Add "Noto Serif SC" to every stack that sets Chinese ("Source Serif 4", "Noto Serif SC", serif) and load the subset that covers the slide's characters (self-hosted subset or unicode-range slices).
findings.why: On Windows the title and kicker mix two Han designs in one line; on a Mac or phone a different system face draws them, so the slide looks different on every machine that presents it.
findings.root: font stacks without a CJK face

findings.title: Content and navigation do not depend on script
findings.where: Both step lists (div.step.show) and output panels, 1920px, tiles/1920-00.png
findings.evidence: resilience.hidden_content.scripts_off: 332 of 640 characters visible (51.9%); the sweep's hidden_content hit (ROB-001, Floor) records 308 characters (48%) invisible with JavaScript off. The steps carry a script-added .show class and the slide has a REPLAY control, so script stages them.
findings.before: The numbered steps on both sides of the comparison appear only when script adds .show.
findings.after: Render the steps visible in the HTML and let script hide and replay them only after it runs (a .js class on html gates the hidden state).
findings.why: A slide exported to PDF, opened in a reader view or shown on a locked-down machine loses the half of the comparison that carries the argument.

strengths: The slide is light: one stylesheet request of 152 KiB and lab LCP 416 ms.
Headings and step text wrap inside their columns; nothing clips at 1920.
html lang is set to zh, matching the main language of the slide.
